sources.entry: NarrateClaude - Hands-free, on-device voice loop for talking to Claude Code: Apple speech recognition in, cloned-voice text-to-speech out, no cloud.

summary.one_liner: NarrateClaude is a macOS hands-free voice loop that transcribes speech on-device with Apple's speech engine, types it into a Terminal window running Claude Code, and reads replies aloud through a user-supplied TTS voice.
summary.what_it_does: The listener (Listen.swift) uses Apple's SFSpeechRecognizer for en-US and treats a sentence as finished when the transcribed text stops changing for 2.5 seconds. A supervisor script (dispatch) respawns the listener, runs a window watchdog, and pipes output through filters into an injector (inject) that types each sentence into the bound Apple Terminal window via AppleScript. A control CLI (dictation) provides setup, start, stop, status, toggle, tail and uninstall commands. Speech playback through afplay pauses recognition to avoid the mic hearing its own replies, and a Claude Code Stop hook (speak-on-stop) reads the last reply aloud via ~/.local/bin/speak. The repo also includes a "was that for me?" filter with tune in/out commands and a local LLM judge that fails open, plus an optional voiceprint filter that the README says is not active in v1. The README describes v1 as the runnable code, while a v2 barge-in effort is documented in logs but its code is not published in this repo.
use_cases: Talk to Claude Code hands-free while walking or cooking
Dictate commands into a Terminal window by voice
Have Claude Code replies read aloud in a cloned voice
Run a fully on-device voice assistant for a local coding model
Voice-control any command-line tool running in Terminal.app
Study echo-cancellation attempts for barge-in in voice agents
how_to_run: Start claude in Apple Terminal.app, then run ./dictation/bin/dictation setup from inside that window
Create ~/.local/bin/speak as a TTS wrapper (README offers a macOS say starter option)
Optionally wrap narrative-claude.sh in a .app bundle for a double-click launcher
stack: Pocket TTS by Kyutai (user's cloned voice, optional)
notable: Ends sentences by watching transcribed text stabilize rather than microphone volume, so noisy rooms still work
Pauses recognition while afplay is playing to prevent the assistant hearing itself
Production hardening: wedge detection, 5-minute preventive respawn, window-ID binding that stops the listener when the Terminal window closes
Engineering log of seven barge-in/echo-cancellation attempts with measured results, including unsuccessful Apple VPIO attempts
Listener is general-purpose and can drive any CLI in Terminal.app, not only Claude Code
caveats: Terminal.app only; iTerm2, Warp and Ghostty are not supported because the injector uses Terminal-specific AppleScript
Half-duplex in v1: no barge-in, and the voiceprint filter is not active with the v1 listener
Requires macOS on Apple Silicon, Microphone and Speech Recognition permissions, and a user-provided TTS setup; fully offline only if claude points at a local model
